provenance.change_summary: Adapted the pinned Bookmark Manager source into a reusable, scenario-fit template (save now, find later). Fixed the category/ tag entry so that comma- or line-separated values typed into the save dialog are committed as chips on input (and re-read from the DOM at submit), which the fixed acceptance plan's `fill`-then-submit flow requires; a link with no category now falls back to the configurable default instead of failing validation. Removed the third-party network calls (microlink metadata, weserv/google favicons) so saving is fully offline and does not store external blobs; records now render a local letter avatar, keeping the end-to-end flow (add, persist, categorise, browse, search, visit/edit/archive/delete) intact. Made the tag input stop shadowing the reactive tag binding, disambiguated the submit button (backdrop close is now type=button), and always showed the header 'Add Bookmark' text. Added src/includes/config.ts with configurable default category, suggested categories and opt-in example data (seeded only when enabled), and tokenised the app name via @@PROJECT_NAME@@ across README.md, index.html, package.json and src/App.tsrx. Pinned the previously 'latest' Ripple/TSRX dependencies to the versions already present in bun.lock for reproducible npm installs. criteria.reason: Persistence: store.ts defines a Dexie/IndexedDB database ('BookmarkDB', version 1 stores 'id, createdAt, visitCount') typed with EntityTable<Bookmark,'id'>. App.tsrx saveBookmark() awaits db.bookmarks.put(bm) and an on-mount effect() calls db.bookmarks.toArray() to reload records, so saved links survive reload/new sessions and accumulate. The Add flow (header button.btn-primary -> dialog with input[type=url], input[placeholder='Website Title Here'], textarea, #bookmark-categories-input, button[type=submit]) matches every plan selector, and submit builds a Bookmark and calls saveBookmark before closing. index.html contains the noscript text 'You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.' and the h2 'All bookmarks' is rendered, matching the http/goto/expect_text checks. Seeding is disabled (appConfig.seedExampleBookmarks=false), so example Bookmark data ('Kitchen Gadget' etc.) does not pre-populate the library and cannot interfere with the checks.

URL anchoring: Bookmark stores url and hostname (hostname computed by getHostname() in utils.ts via new URL().hostname) and each article renders {item.hostname}, so 'shop.example.com'/'blog.example.org' appear. The per-card actions button has class including 'btn-circle' and popovertarget={'popover-actions-'+item.id}, and its popover menu id is 'popover-actions-'+item.id, matching the selectors. The 'Visit' action calls window.open(item.url,'_blank','noopener,noreferrer'), returning to the anchored page URL (https://shop.example.com/kitchen-gadget) as required by the open_link check. Runtime jump itself was not executed.

Category creation/re-filing: categories are the Bookmark.tags array; parseCategories() adds trimmed, deduped categories and the submit handler defaults empty input to appConfig.defaultCategory. Creating a bookmark with gift-ideas renders the tag badge and aside category entry (expect_text gift-ideas), and the Dexie put makes it survive reload. Editing opens the dialog with draftTags=[...item.tags]; the badge's remove button (draftTags.filter) drops gift-ideas, then filling #bookmark-categories-input with home-ideas and submitting yields tags ['home-ideas'] with the same id, calls saveBookmark (persisted), shows the success toast 'Bookmark updated', and a reload re-reads home-ideas from IndexedDB. All plan selectors for this flow (article popover button, menu Edit, dialog .badge button, #bookmark-categories-input, button[type=submit]) exist in the markup.

Retrieval by category and keyword: the aside renders a checkbox per category with value={category} bound via bindGroup(filtersRef); the derived bookmarks list filters by _tags.every(t => bookmark.tags.includes(t)), so checking aside input[type=checkbox][value='home-ideas'] narrows the list to 'Living Room Repaint'. The header input[type='search'] is bound via bindValue(searchRef) and the same derived list filters on bookmark.title.toLowerCase().includes(_search), so searching 'Kitchen' shows 'Kitchen Gadget' and 'Desk' shows 'Desk Lamp'. Tab, filter, sort, and search are all reactive track() values, so the filtering recomputes as inputs change.
